name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Turkish lira near record low of 50.2 per dollar under managed depreciation; no major EM default or capital controls
state: The Turkish lira was near 50.2 per dollar on 10 Nov, a record low but only 1.9% weaker over a month, as authorities manage the pace of depreciation (Trading Economics). Paraguay's central bank put Ueno Bank into resolution in early November and President Peña announced his resignation (Al Jazeera, 6 Nov), but Paraguay is not a major emerging economy. No major emerging economy had defaulted, imposed capital controls or sought emergency IMF support as of 10 Nov.
for_you: Emerging-market stress can affect funds and pensions with exposure to those countries. Current moves are gradual rather than a crisis.
rubric_hit: No major EM currency fall > 10% in a month, default or emergency IMF request

sources.title: Al Jazeera — How Paraguay's Ueno collapse is only its latest banking crisis

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
